claim: A screen of itch-inducing compounds (pruritogens) in zebrafish larvae yielded a single pruritogen, the TLR7 agonist imiquimod, that elicited a somatosensory neuron response.
source: A screen of itch-inducing compounds (pruritogens) in zebrafish larvae yielded a single pruritogen, the TLR7 agonist imiquimod, that elicited a somatosensory neuron response.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and it is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 where imiquimod activated trigeminal neurons.

claim: Imiquimod induced itch-like behaviors in zebrafish distinct from those induced by the noxious TRPA1 agonist, allyl isothiocyanate.
source: Imiquimod induced itch-like behaviors in zebrafish distinct from those induced by the noxious TRPA1 agonist, allyl isothiocyanate.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figure 1 showing distinct behavioral responses (lip-rubbing vs. freezing) to IMQ vs. AITC.

claim: In the zebrafish, imiquimod-evoked somatosensory neuronal responses and behaviors were entirely dependent upon TRPA1.
source: In the zebrafish, imiquimod-evoked somatosensory neuronal responses and behaviors were entirely dependent upon TRPA1
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2 showing that trpa1b-/- zebrafish showed no neuronal or behavioral responses to IMQ.

claim: In the mouse TRPA1 was required for the direct activation of somatosensory neurons by imiquimod.
source: while in the mouse TRPA1 was required for the direct activation of somatosensory neurons
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data in Figure 5 showing that Trpa1-/- mouse DRG neurons did not respond to IMQ.

claim: In the mouse, TRPA1 was partially responsible for behaviors elicited by imiquimod.
source: while in the mouse TRPA1 was required for the direct activation of somatosensory neurons and partially responsible for behaviors elicited by this pruritogen.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figure 5 showing that Trpa1-/- mice had attenuated but not abolished scratching responses to low-dose IMQ.

claim: Imiquimod was found to be a direct but weak TRPA1 agonist.
source: Imiquimod was found to be a direct but weak TRPA1 agonist
evidence: This is supported by heterologous expression data in Figure 3 showing IMQ directly activates TRPA1 in HEK cells with higher EC50 values than AITC.

claim: Imiquimod activated a subset of TRPA1 expressing neurons.
source: Imiquimod was found to be a direct but weak TRPA1 agonist that activated a subset of TRPA1 expressing neurons.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data in Figure 4 showing that only 28% of AITC+ neurons also responded to IMQ.

claim: Imiquimod-responsive TRPA1 expressing neurons were significantly more sensitive to noxious stimuli than other TRPA1 expressing neurons.
source: Imiquimod-responsive TRPA1 expressing neurons were significantly more sensitive to noxious stimuli than other TRPA1 expressing neurons.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4D and Figure 5H showing that IMQ+/AITC+ neurons had significantly higher maximum responses to AITC than AITC+ only neurons.

claim: Itch is an unpleasant sensation that elicits a scratch behavior in terrestrial vertebrates.
source: Itch is an unpleasant sensation that elicits a scratch behavior in terrestrial vertebrates.
evidence: This is a general statement about itch that draws from established scientific knowledge.

claim: In mammals, chemically-induced itch is thought to be mediated by pruritic receptors on somatosensory neurons.
source: In mammals, chemically-induced itch is thought to be mediated by pruritic receptors on somatosensory neurons (Bautista et al., 2014; Hoon, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pruritic receptors are typically G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) that, upon activation, prompt the opening of downstream transient receptor potential (TRP) channels.
source: These receptors are typically G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) that, upon activation, prompt the opening of downstream transient receptor potential (TRP) channels, facilitating activation of the neuron (Ross, 2011; Zhang, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TRPA1 and TRPV1 serve as nociceptors, mediating responses to algogenic (painful) stimuli.
source: This coupling of pruritic receptors to TRPA1 or TRPV1 is especially intriguing in that these TRP channels also serve as nociceptors, mediating responses to algogenic (painful) stimuli (Laing and Dhaka, 2016; Ikoma et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) have proven to be a valuable tool in the study of nociception.
source: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) have proven to be a valuable tool in the study of nociception (Gau et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The zebrafish ortholog of Trpa1, trpa1b, is required for nociceptive responses to aversive pungent chemicals.
source: The zebrafish ortholog of Trpa1, trpa1b, is required for nociceptive responses to aversive pungent chemicals (Prober et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Orthologs of genes involved in mammalian itch transduction are present in the zebrafish.
source: Orthologs of genes involved in mammalian itch transduction are also present in the zebrafish (Kaslin and Panula, 2001; Pei et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Of the pruritogens screened, only imiquimod (IMQ) significantly (p<0.05) activated zebrafish trigeminal ganglia (TG) neurons.
source: Of the pruritogens screened, only imiquimod (IMQ) significantly (p<0.05) activated zebrafish trigeminal ganglia (TG) neurons (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by CaMPARI imaging data shown in Figure 1I demonstrating significant neuronal activation only with IMQ treatment.

claim: Only IMQ elevated baseline locomotion (p<0.001) in 5dpf larval zebrafish when exposed to individual pruritogens.
source: When 5dpf larval zebrafish were exposed to individual pruritogens, only IMQ elevated baseline locomotion (p<0.001), producing a dose dependent increase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1J and dose-response data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Injection of IMQ into the lip elicited a lip-rubbing behavior in adult zebrafish that was absent in sham-injected control fish (p<0.001).
source: Injection of IMQ into the lip elicited a lip-rubbing behavior that may constitute a form of itch-scratch response in zebrafish, a behavior that was absent in sham-injected control fish (p<0.001) (Figure 1K,L; Videos 1—3)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1L and Videos 1-3.

claim: Injection of AITC produced freezing behavior (p<0.01) in adult zebrafish.
source: Consistent with studies of nocifensive behaviors, injection of AITC produced freezing behavior (p<0.01) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Injection of AITC produced a significant decrease (p<0.05) in velocity in adult zebrafish not observed in control or IMQ injected fish.
source: as well as a significant decrease (p<0.05) in velocity not observed in control or IMQ injected fish (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IMQ, a treatment for various skin disorders, acts through TLR7 to stimulate an immune response.
source: IMQ, a treatment for various skin disorders, acts through TLR7 to stimulate an immune response, with intense itching and painful burning commonly reported as side effects (Chang et al., 2005; Lebwohl et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In mice, IMQ is reported to be itch selective, and only elicits scratching, but not nociceptive, behaviors.
source: In mice, however, IMQ is reported to be itch selective, and only elicits scratching, but not nociceptive, behaviors (Liu et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: One study found that Tlr7-/- mice showed deficits in IMQ evoked itch and proposed that Tlr7 expressed in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons was mediating IMQ transduction.
source: One study found that Tlr7-/- mice showed deficits in IMQ evoked itch and proposed that Tlr7 expressed in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons was mediating IMQ transduction (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: TLR7 has been reported to couple with TRPA1 in DRG neurons to evoke nociception in response to other TLR7 agonists.
source: TLR7 has also been reported to couple with TRPA1 in DRG neurons to evoke nociception in response to other TLR7 agonists (Park et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Conflicting studies found that Tlr7-/- mice exhibited no deficits in IMQ-evoked itch.
source: However, conflicting studies found that Tlr7-/- mice exhibited no deficits in IMQ-evoked itch, and RNAseq analysis of DRG neurons found no evidence for Tlr7 expression (Kim et al., 2011; Usoskin et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RNAseq analysis of DRG neurons found no evidence for Tlr7 expression.
source: However, conflicting studies found that Tlr7-/- mice exhibited no deficits in IMQ-evoked itch, and RNAseq analysis of DRG neurons found no evidence for Tlr7 expression (Kim et al., 2011; Usoskin et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: tlr7 mRNA expression is restricted to known hematopoietic regions in larval zebrafish.
source: In situ hybridization studies in zebrafish larvae revealed that tlr7 mRNA expression is restricted to known hematopoietic regions in larval zebrafish (Bresciani, 2014; Du et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and citations to previous literature.

claim: tlr7 mRNA expression was notably absent in both TG and Rohon-Beard (RB) neurons in zebrafish larvae.
source: and was notably absent in both TG and Rohon-Beard (RB) neurons (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claim: trpa1b expression was observed in both TG and RB neurons in zebrafish larvae.
source: As expected, trpa1b expression was observed in both TG and RB neurons (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Tlr7-/- zebrafish larvae exhibited a significant (p<0.001) increase in total locomotion when exposed to IMQ (100 µM) that was indistinguishable from controls.
source: Tlr7-/- zebrafish larvae exhibited a significant (p<0.001) increase in total locomotion when exposed to IMQ (100 µM) that was indistinguishable from controls (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: trpa1b-/- larvae demonstrated no response to IMQ (100 µM), while their WT siblings displayed normal IMQ induced behaviors (p<0.01).
source: However, trpa1b-/- larvae demonstrated no response to IMQ (100 µM), while their WT siblings displayed normal IMQ induced behaviors (p<0.01, Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Behavioral responses to AITC were absent in trpa1b-/- fish.
source: As expected based on previous reports, behavioral responses to AITC were absent in trpa1b-/- fish (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) (Prober et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F and a citation to previous literature.

claim: trpa1b-/- fish demonstrated an equivalent increase in locomotor behavior as their WT siblings when exposed to increased temperatures.
source: Notably, trpa1b-/- fish demonstrated an equivalent increase in locomotor behavior as their WT siblings when exposed to increased temperatures (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In WT larvae, IMQ activation was seen exclusively in a subset of AITC responsive neurons (4/36, n = 5 larvae).
source: In WT larvae, IMQ activation was seen exclusively in a subset of AITC responsive neurons (4/36, n = 5 larvae).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Trpa1b-/- fish exhibited no response to either IMQ or AITC (0/89 total neurons, n = 5 larvae).
source: Trpa1b-/- fish, however, exhibited no response to either IMQ or AITC (0/89 total neurons, n = 5 larvae) (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The highly specific TLR7 agonist loxoribine did not evoke TG neuron activation, larval locomotion, or adult lip-rubbing behavior in zebrafish.
source: Notably, the highly specific TLR7 agonist loxoribine did not evoke TG neuron activation, larval locomotion, or adult lip-rubbing behavior, further strengthening the finding that Tlr7 does not play a role in IMQ evoked behaviors in zebrafish (Figure 1I,J; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1I, 1J, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Loxoribine does not elicit pruritic behavioral responses in mice.
source: This finding is similar to reports in the mouse demonstrating that loxoribine does not elicit pruritic behavioral responses (Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: HEK cells transfected with zebrafish, mouse, and human Trpa1 showed a dose-dependent increase in intracellular calcium following application of IMQ and AITC that was not observed in HEK cells alone.
source: HEK cells transfected with zebrafish, mouse, and human Trpa1 showed a dose-dependent increase in intracellular calcium following application of IMQ and AITC that was not observed in HEK cells alone (Figure 3A–F; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3A-F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: Loxoribine did not activate HEK cells transfected with zebrafish or mouse Trpa1.
source: Importantly, we found that loxoribine did not activate HEK cells transfected with zebrafish or mouse Trpa1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D)
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: When stimulated with IMQ, voltage-clamped HEK cells transfected with mouse or zebrafish Trpa1 demonstrated a significant increase in current.
source: When stimulated with IMQ, voltage-clamped HEK cells transfected with mouse or zebrafish Trpa1 demonstrated a significant increase in current (Figure 3G; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Co-transfecting mouse Tlr7 with mouse Trpa1 in HEK cells had no demonstrable effect on current influx.
source: Co-transfecting mouse Tlr7 with mouse Trpa1 in HEK cells had no demonstrable effect on current influx (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: No difference was found in the IMQ current density dose-response curves for cells transfected with zebrafish trpa1b, mouse Trpa1, or mouse Trpa1 + mouse Tlr7.
source: Additionally, no difference was found in the IMQ current density dose-response curves for cells transfected with zebrafish trpa1b, mouse Trpa1, or mouse Trpa1 + mouse Tlr7 (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: No evidence was found that TLR7 coupled with TRPA1 in the presence of loxoribine as measured by ratiometric calcium imaging and whole cell electrophysiology in mouse and zebrafish.
source: In contrast to previous reports, we found no evidence that TLR7 coupled with TRPA1 in the presence of loxoribine as measured by ratiometric calcium imaging and whole cell electrophysiology in mouse and zebrafish (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D) (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D and contrasts with a cited previous report.

claim: Zebrafish Tlr7 did not respond to either IMQ or loxoribine in a dual-luciferase assay.
source: Intriguingly, zebrafish Tlr7 did not respond to either IMQ or loxoribine in a dual-luciferase assay, suggesting that zebrafish Tlr7 is not activated by mammalian TLR7 agonists (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by dual-luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The EC50 of IMQ for zebrafish, mouse and human TRPA1 was consistently higher than the AITC EC50.
source: The EC50 of IMQ for zebrafish, mouse and human TRPA1 was consistently higher than the AITC EC50, demonstrating that IMQ is a weaker agonist than AITC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 3D-F and summarized in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: The IMQ EC50 of zebrafish Trpa1 and human TRPA1 were only 2–3 fold greater than that of the EC50 of AITC.
source: Notably, while the IMQ EC50 of zebrafish Trpa1 and human TRPA1 were only 2–3 fold greater than that of the EC50 of AITC
evidence: This is supported by EC50 values shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Mouse TRPA1 demonstrated a ~40 fold difference between the EC50 of AITC and IMQ.
source: mouse TRPA1 demonstrated a ~40 fold difference between the EC50 of AITC and IMQ.
evidence: This is supported by EC50 values shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K.

claim: HEK cells transfected with zebrafish trpa1b exhibited identical current density responses upon stimulation with the maximum dose of either AITC or IMQ.
source: In similar electrophysiology experiments, HEK cells transfected with zebrafish trpa1b exhibited identical current density responses upon stimulation with the maximum dose of either AITC or IMQ
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Cells transfected with mouse Trpa1 exhibited significantly higher current density responses following stimulation with AITC, relative to IMQ.
source: but cells transfected with mouse Trpa1 exhibited significantly higher current density responses following stimulation with AITC, relative to IMQ (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: No IMQ+/AITC- neurons were found across 13 larvae.
source: No IMQ+/AITC- neurons were found across 13 larvae.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data in elavl3:H2BGCaMP6 transgenic zebrafish.

claim: Among AITC+ neurons, 28% (31/111) were responsive to IMQ.
source: Among AITC+ neurons, 28% (31/111) were responsive to IMQ (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Application of 100 μM IMQ elicited a lower maximal ΔF/F response than application of 50 μM AITC in IMQ+/AITC+ TG neurons in 3dpf larval zebrafish.
source: In IMQ+/AITC+ neurons, we determined that the average maximum fluorescence intensity response to the IMQ stimulus was significantly lower than that of the AITC stimulus (p<0.001), implying that at the concentrations used, IMQ is indeed a weaker TRPA1 stimulus than AITC in vivo (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The maximum AITC response of IMQ+/AITC+ neurons was significantly greater than that of AITC+ only neurons.
source: Furthermore, we found that the maximum AITC response of IMQ+/AITC+ neurons was significantly greater than that of AITC+ only neurons (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IMQ+/AITC+ neurons displayed a significantly greater average AITC response than AITC+ only neurons (p<0.05).
source: Likewise, IMQ+/AITC+ neurons displayed a significantly greater average AITC response than AITC+ only neurons (p<0.05, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Of the IMQ+ neurons identified across five fish, 92.3% (12/13) responded to both pulses of IMQ.
source: Of the IMQ+ neurons we identified across five fish, 92.3% (12/13) responded to both pulses of IMQ, whereas only 7.7% (1/13) responded only to the second pulse of IMQ (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Decreasing the concentration of applied AITC correlated with a reduction in the number of photoconverted neurons.
source: In CaMPARI fish we observed that decreasing the concentration of applied AITC correlated with a reduction in the number of photoconverted neurons (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by CaMPARI imaging data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Administering higher IMQ concentrations converts an equivalent number of neurons as high concentrations of AITC.
source: Additionally, administering higher IMQ concentrations converts an equivalent number of neurons as high concentrations of AITC (Figure 4E)
evidence: This is supported by CaMPARI imaging data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Only a subset of neurons that responded to a high concentration (50 μM) of AITC responded to a lower concentration (10 μM) of AITC (11/42).
source: In vivo GCaMP imaging bolstered our CaMPARI findings that stimulus intensity affects which subpopulations of Trpa1+ neurons are activated. In these experiments, we observed that increasing the stimulus intensity activated more neurons. Only a subset of neurons that responded to a high concentration (50 μM) of AITC responded to a lower concentration (10 μM) of AITC (11/42)
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Of neurons that responded to 10 μM AITC, even fewer neurons responded to 100 μM IMQ (4/11).
source: and of those even fewer neurons responded to 100 μM IMQ (4/11) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Increasing the IMQ concentration to 200 µM in adult behavioral experiments evoked nocifensive behaviors such as elevated freezing and significantly reduced velocity.
source: Furthermore, increasing the IMQ concentration to 200 µM in adult behavioral experiments evoked nocifensive behaviors such as elevated freezing and significantly reduced velocity, and the itch-like lip rubbing behavior seen at 100 µM was notably absent (Maximino, 2011; Sneddon, 2009) (Figure 4F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, along with citations to previous literature.

claim: Low concentrations of AITC (5 μM) elicited both itch-like lip rubbing behavior and increased velocity.
source: Conversely, low concentrations of AITC (5 μM) elicited both itch-like lip rubbing behavior and increased velocity (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: IMQ elicited responses in 9.6% (83/864) of cultured AITC+ DRG neurons from WT animals.
source: We found that IMQ elicited responses in 9.6% (83/864) of cultured AITC+ DRG neurons (Figure 5A) from WT animals.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Both IMQ and AITC responses were completely abolished in DRG neurons obtained from Trpa1-/- animals.
source: We found that both IMQ and AITC responses were completely abolished in DRG neurons obtained from Trpa1-/- animals, while neurons from WT siblings exhibited normal responsivity to both stimuli (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Application of loxoribine did not elicit calcium responses in mouse DRG neurons.
source: Furthermore, application of loxoribine did not elicit calcium responses in mouse DRG neurons, providing evidence that TLR7 stimulation does not result in activation of somatosensory neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1H.

claim: High-dose IMQ (125 μg) paw injections did not evoke nocifensive behaviors in WT mice (n = 0/10 IMQ-injected).
source: High-dose IMQ (125 μg) paw injections did not evoke nocifensive behaviors in WT mice (n = 0/10 IMQ-injected), consistent with previous reports (Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Scratching bouts at a low concentration of IMQ (10 μg, nape injected) were significantly attenuated in Trpa1-/- mice.
source: However, scratching bouts at a low concentration of IMQ (10 μg, nape injected) were significantly attenuated in Trpa1-/- mice, demonstrating that TRPA1 is required for normal IMQ-induced scratching behavior (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A higher dose of IMQ (50 μg) evoked equivalent scratching behavior in both WT and Trpa1-/- mice.
source: Interestingly, a higher dose of IMQ (50 μg) evoked equivalent scratching behavior in both WT and Trpa1-/- mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The vast majority of IMQ+ neurons (73%, 23/30) also responded to the TRPA1-dependent pruritogens deoxycholic acid (DC) and chloroquine (CQ).
source: We found that the vast majority of IMQ+ neurons (73%, 23/30) also responded to these pruritic stimuli (Figure 5G)
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5E-G.

claim: Increasing the concentration of AITC activated more DRG neurons in a dose-dependent manner in the mouse.
source: In the mouse, increasing the concentration of AITC activated more DRG neurons in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Within the population of neurons that responded to lower concentrations of AITC, the IMQ+ subpopulation was enriched.
source: Furthermore, within the population of neurons that responded to lower concentrations of AITC, the IMQ+ subpopulation was enriched (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1J.

claim: IMQ+ neurons in the mouse had a smaller peak responses to IMQ than AITC.
source: We also found that IMQ+ neurons in the mouse had a smaller peak responses to IMQ than AITC (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: AITC peak responses within the IMQ+ population were significantly greater than in the AITC+ only population (p<0.01).
source: Additionally, AITC peak responses within the IMQ+ population were significantly greater than in the AITC+ only population (p<0.01), demonstrating that the heightened sensitivity of IMQ+ neurons to TRPA1 agonists is conserved in the mouse (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: IMQ+ DRG neurons exhibited a significantly higher maximum response to the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin (CAPS) than CAPS+ only neurons.
source: Subsequent experiments revealed that IMQ+ DRG neurons exhibited a significantly higher maximum response to the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin (CAPS) than CAPS+ only neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–F)
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: AITC (50 mM) produces significant scratching behavior with no appreciable wiping behavior (p<0.001 and N.S. respectively) in mice.
source: We observed that AITC (50 mM) produces significant scratching behavior with no appreciable wiping behavior (p<0.001 and N.S. respectively)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: A higher dose of AITC (100 mM) results in a significant attenuation of the observed scratching behavior, as well as a significant wiping behavior (p<0.05 and p<0.001 respectively) in mice.
source: while a higher dose of AITC (100 mM) results in a significant attenuation of the observed scratching behavior, as well as a significant wiping behavior (p<0.05 and p<0.001 respectively) (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: IMQ can elicit behavior and neuronal responses in zebrafish.
source: Through a combination of experimental procedures, we show that the pruritogen IMQ can elicit behavior and neuronal responses in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: In larvae, IMQ elicits an increase in locomotion and activation of somatosensory TG neurons.
source: In larvae, IMQ elicits an increase in locomotion and activation of somatosensory TG neurons
evidence: This is supported by behavioral and imaging data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In adult zebrafish, peripherally applied IMQ produces a scratching-analogous lip-rubbing behavioral response that is distinct from the nocifensive behaviors evoked by the algogen AITC.
source: Furthermore, in adult zebrafish, peripherally applied IMQ produces a scratching-analogous lip-rubbing behavioral response that is distinct from the nocifensive behaviors evoked by the algogen AITC as well as previously described escape behaviors (Correia et al., 2011; Maximino, 2011; Colwill and Creton, 2011; Egan et al., 2009; Levin et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1 and citations to previous literature.

claim: TLR7 is not involved in the direct activation of somatosensory neurons by IMQ.
source: Our work provides additional evidence that TLR7 is not involved in the direct activation of somatosensory neurons by IMQ (Kim et al., 2011; Usoskin et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental results in the manuscript and citations to previous literature.

claim: The TRPA1 ion channel plays a key role in transducing IMQ-evoked neuronal effects and the behaviors that result from such neuronal activity.
source: Instead, the TRPA1 ion channel appears to play a key role in transducing IMQ-evoked neuronal effects and the behaviors that result from such neuronal activity.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental results showing TRPA1 dependence of IMQ responses.

claim: IMQ was able to directly activate TRPA1.
source: Utilizing both electrophysiology and calcium imaging, we showed that IMQ was able to directly activate TRPA1
evidence: This is supported by heterologous expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Co-transfection of Tlr7 did not potentiate IMQ-evoked responses.
source: and that co-transfection of Tlr7 did not potentiate IMQ-evoked responses.
evidence: This is supported by heterologous expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: With zebrafish and human TRPA1, IMQ eventually reached the same maximal calcium response levels as AITC.
source: With zebrafish and human TRPA1, IMQ eventually reached the same maximal calcium response levels as AITC
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: IMQ responses with mouse TRPA1 plateaued at lower maximal levels than AITC.
source: while IMQ responses with mouse TRPA1 plateaued at lower maximal levels than AITC.
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: In the context of TRPA1 activation, stronger stimuli elicited nocifensive behaviors, whereas weaker stimuli evoked pruritic behaviors.
source: In the context of TRPA1 activation, stronger stimuli elicited nocifensive behaviors, whereas weaker stimuli evoked pruritic behaviors.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Low concentrations of IMQ evoked pruritic behaviors while higher concentrations of IMQ were capable of eliciting nocifensive freezing behaviors in adult zebrafish.
source: In adult zebrafish low concentrations of IMQ evoked pruritic behaviors while higher concentrations of IMQ were capable of eliciting nocifensive freezing behaviors.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Low concentrations of AITC produced scratching behaviors, while higher concentrations of AITC evoked nocifensive behaviors in both zebrafish and mice.
source: Low concentrations of AITC produced scratching behaviors, while higher concentrations of AITC evoked nocifensive behaviors in both species.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 5I.

claim: Experiments with two different calcium indicators of neuronal activity, GCaMP and CaMPARI, revealed a correlation between TRPA1 agonist stimulus intensity and neuronal recruitment.
source: Experiments with two different calcium indicators of neuronal activity, GCaMP and CaMPARI, revealed a correlation between TRPA1 agonist stimulus intensity and neuronal recruitment.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Stronger stimuli (high concentrations of TRPA1 agonists) activated more neurons than weaker stimuli (lower concentrations of TRPA1 agonists).
source: Specifically, stronger stimuli (high concentrations of TRPA1 agonists) activated more neurons than weaker stimuli (lower concentrations of TRPA1 agonists).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Calcium imaging of zebrafish and mouse somatosensory neurons revealed the existence of at least two functionally distinct neuronal subpopulations.
source: Calcium imaging of zebrafish and mouse somatosensory neurons revealed the existence of at least two functionally distinct neuronal subpopulations.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: A population of neurons responded to both low and high intensity TRPA1 agonists and another population only responded to high intensity TRPA1 agonists.
source: In both species, we observed a population of neurons that responded to both low and high intensity TRPA1 agonists and another that only responded to high intensity TRPA1 agonists.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Sequential pulses of IMQ (100 μM) activate the low intensity TRPA1 agonist responsive population in zebrafish, demonstrating that this population is likely genetically defined, and not determined stochastically.
source: Our observation that sequential pulses of IMQ (100 μM) activate the low intensity TRPA1 agonist responsive population in zebrafish demonstrates that this population is likely genetically defined, and not determined stochastically.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the mouse, the vast majority of IMQ (100 μM) responsive neurons also responded to the TRPA1-dependent pruritogens chloroquine and deoxycholic acid.
source: Furthermore, in the mouse, we observed that the vast majority of IMQ (100 μM) responsive neurons also responded to the TRPA1-dependent pruritogens chloroquine and deoxycholic acid
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5E-G.

claim: In both zebrafish and mice, neurons that responded to low intensity TRPA1 agonists exhibited a greater response to high intensity AITC stimulation than neurons that only responded to high intensity AITC stimulation.
source: In alignment with these results, in both species, neurons that responded to low intensity TRPA1 agonists also exhibited a greater response to high intensity AITC stimulation than neurons that only responded to high intensity AITC stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 5H.

claim: Putative itch-encoding neurons comprise a more sensitive subset of somatosensory neurons than nociceptive neurons.
source: This implies that putative itch-encoding neurons comprise a more sensitive subset of somatosensory neurons than nociceptive neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that IMQ+ neurons have higher responses to AITC than AITC+ only neurons.

claim: In both species, IMQ (100 μM) responsive neurons were enriched within populations of neurons that responded to low concentrations of AITC.
source: Additionally, in both species, IMQ (100 μM) responsive neurons were enriched within populations of neurons that responded to low concentrations of AITC
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1J.

claim: Weak stimuli such as lower concentrations of the TRPA1 agonists IMQ and AITC activate only a subset of highly sensitive pruriceptive TRPA1-expressing neurons.
source: Weak stimuli such as lower concentrations of the TRPA1 agonists IMQ and AITC activate only a subset of highly sensitive pruriceptive TRPA1-expressing neurons
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The remaining nociceptive TRPA1-expressing neurons are only recruited by higher intensity TRPA1 stimuli.
source: while the remaining nociceptive TRPA1-expressing neurons are only recruited by higher intensity TRPA1 stimuli.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: IMQ-induced itch was attenuated, but not abolished, in Trpa1-/- mice.
source: Our findings that IMQ-induced itch was attenuated, but not abolished, in Trpa1-/- mice supports additional mechanisms for IMQ-evoked itch in this species.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The activation of an immune response by IMQ in other cell types could result in a cascade of downstream signaling that could ultimately lead to a release of endogenous pruritic stimuli.
source: One may speculate that the activation of an immune response by IMQ in other cell types could result in a cascade of downstream signaling that could ultimately lead to a release of endogenous pruritic stimuli (e.g. histamine and serotonin from mast cells).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claim: In the zebrafish, TLR7 is unlikely to contribute even indirectly to IMQ-induced itch sensation, as no behavioral phenotype was observed in tlr7-/- animals.
source: In the zebrafish, TLR7 is unlikely to contribute even indirectly to IMQ-induced itch sensation, as we observed no behavioral phenotype in tlr7-/- animals.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Pathogen exposure could stimulate the immune system via TLR activation or other pathways, leading to an indirect activation of pruritic somatosensory neurons and triggering both itch sensations and scratching behaviors.
source: However, this does not rule out the possibility that pathogen exposure could stimulate the immune system via TLR activation or other pathways, leading to an indirect activation of pruritic somatosensory neurons and triggering both itch sensations and scratching behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claim: Several studies have implicated that Tlrs in several species of fish play a role in immunity.
source: Several studies have implicated that Tlrs in several species of fish play a role in immunity (Meijer et al., 2004; Kanwal et al., 2014; Zhou and Sun, 2015; Tanekhy et al., 2010; Kileng et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Out of several mammalian pruritogens, only IMQ elicited behavioral and neuronal responses in zebrafish.
source: We observed that out of several mammalian pruritogens, only IMQ elicited behavioral and neuronal responses in zebrafish.
evidence: This is supported by screening data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Histamine, serotonin, TGR5, and PAR-2 receptors may not function in the itch pathway as pruritic receptors on primary sensory neurons in zebrafish, as they do in mammals.
source: It is likewise possible that histamine, serotonin, TGR5, and PAR-2 receptors do not function in the itch pathway as pruritic receptors on primary sensory neurons in zebrafish, as they do in mammals.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the lack of response to these pruritogens in zebrafish.

claim: Zebrafish have an extensive histaminergic system with multiple histamine receptors, but histamine receptor expression appears to be restricted to the central nervous system.
source: For example, zebrafish have an extensive histaminergic system with multiple histamine receptors, but histamine receptor expression appears to be restricted to the central nervous system (Peitsaro et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Studies indicate that zebrafish mast cells do not contain histamine or serotonin.
source: Furthermore, while zebrafish do possess mast cells (which in mammals release histamine and serotonin that act upon peripheral sensory neurons to elicit itch), studies indicate that these mast cells do not contain histamine or serotonin (Prykhozhij and Berman, 2014; Mulero et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the zebrafish, histamine and serotonin may not play a functional role in pruritic sensation or immune responses, but are restricted to more central processes such as mediating sleep-wakefulness cycles, mood, and anxiety.
source: It is therefore plausible that in the zebrafish, histamine and serotonin do not play a functional role in pruritic sensation or immune responses, but are restricted to more central processes such as mediating sleep-wakefulness cycles, mood, and anxiety (Pei et al., 2016; Sackerman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The direct activation of a TRP channel to elicit itch or pain through the recruitment of distinct populations of somatosensory neurons via stimulus sensitivity is mechanistically simple.
source: The direct activation of a TRP channel to elicit itch or pain through the recruitment of distinct populations of somatosensory neurons via stimulus sensitivity is mechanistically simple.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement about the proposed mechanism.

claim: The presence of this mechanism in both zebrafish and mouse may imply that this particular form of itch transduction appeared before the emergence of terrestrial vertebrates, and may have been conserved throughout evolutionary history to persist in mammals.
source: That such a mechanism is present in both zebrafish and mouse may imply that this particular form of itch transduction appeared before the emergence of terrestrial vertebrates, and may have been conserved throughout evolutionary history to persist in mammals.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary conservation.

claim: This rudimentary form of itch potentially evolved from existing pain-transducing molecular and neural machinery as a means to differentiate high- and low-intensity noxious stimuli for which an alternative behavioral response was more appropriate.
source: One could therefore postulate that this rudimentary form of itch potentially evolved from existing pain-transducing molecular and neural machinery as a means to differentiate high- and low-intensity noxious stimuli for which an alternative behavioral response was more appropriate.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary origins.

claim: IMQ can directly activate TRPA1 to elicit pruritic behavioral responses in both the zebrafish and mouse.
source: Our work demonstrates that IMQ can directly activate TRPA1 to elicit pruritic behavioral responses in both the zebrafish and mouse.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings supported by multiple experimental results.

claim: The immune receptor TLR7 does not mediate somatosensory neuronal responses to IMQ.
source: Furthermore, we have shown that the immune receptor TLR7 does not mediate somatosensory neuronal responses to IMQ.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results.

claim: In both zebrafish and mice, a subset of highly sensitive TRPA1-expressing itch-encoding neurons can respond to weaker TRPA1 agonists to encode sensations of itch and elicit discrete itch behaviors.
source: Our results imply that in both species a subset of highly sensitive TRPA1-expressing itch-encoding neurons can respond to weaker TRPA1 agonists to encode sensations of itch and elicit discrete itch behaviors.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results.

claim: More intense stimuli, such as those that evoke nocifensive behaviors, appear to recruit the highly-sensitive subset as well as less-sensitive TRPA1-expressing neurons.
source: More intense stimuli, such as those that evoke nocifensive behaviors, appear to recruit this highly-sensitive subset as well as less-sensitive TRPA1-expressing neurons.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results.

claim: IMQ responsive neurons in the mouse are part of a TRPA1-expressing subpopulation that is activated by other TRPA1 dependent pruritogens.
source: Our finding that IMQ responsive neurons in the mouse are part of a TRPA1-expressing subpopulation that is activated by other TRPA1 dependent pruritogens provides further evidence that these more sensitive neurons indeed signal itch.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5E-G.

claim: Parallel observations between the zebrafish and mouse suggest that this relatively simple mechanism for conveying, and distinguishing between, pruritic and algogenic stimuli originated early in vertebrate evolution and appears to be preserved in mammals.
source: Parallel observations between the zebrafish and mouse suggest that this relatively simple mechanism for conveying, and distinguishing between, pruritic and algogenic stimuli originated early in vertebrate evolution and appears to be preserved in mammals.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary conservation based on the parallel findings in zebrafish and mice.

claim: The results support the existence of a population-coding based strategy through which differential activation of TRPA1-expressing somatosensory neurons with high or low sensitivities to TRPA1 agonists can relay the discrete sensations of itch and pain respectively.
source: In sum, our results support the existence of a population-coding based strategy through which differential activation of TRPA1-expressing somatosensory neurons with high or low sensitivities to TRPA1 agonists can relay the discrete sensations of itch and pain respectively.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the proposed model supported by multiple experimental results.
